claims.statement: Retiring O24 preserves old recovery history without recording new notifications or triggering outgoing work.

The native bridge retains installed-plugin observations but rejects plugin list/read/install/reconcile management and MCP configuration reload; historical plugin state is still persisted as observations.
The skill picker projects only enabled native skills for the selected workspace, preserves exact skill paths, and does not install or enable plugin candidates.
The desktop offers explicit source-preserving native branch choices alongside same-thread edits and keeps branch input as a canonical draft until a separate send.
Imported ChatGPT PAT accounts use identity verified by the native whoami authority and retain no synthetic OAuth refresh token or expiry.
Exact tool and file-change details use the current native item-read API without an older-server history fallback.

Native prediction forks are explicit ephemeral client capabilities that inherit parent context and tools and reuse bounded temporary-turn cleanup; they do not implement automatic prediction or replace isolated recaps.
Native root-conversation read receipts are source-bound and independent of local handoff state; reading does not acknowledge results and stale marks are not retried.

Background compaction and selected delegation-output retention use the existing Context defaults controls and native config.toml. Omitted values follow native feature defaults; explicit effective configuration and off values retain priority. Saved user and effective project values remain separate, and saving defaults does not restart loaded conversations.
Recorded instruction delivery requests retention only for work_instruction outputs; wakes, capacity retries and injected evidence remain unselected and retain application authority.

The native defaults panel exposes async compaction, client tool-output retention and per-user-configured-server catalog readiness. It does not expose or admit writes to multi_agent_v2.disable_native_tools; production launch arguments do not force that option.
Account admission accepts only the native plus, pro, prolite, promax and team plans, case-insensitively; absent and unknown plans remain unsupported.

The fixed native launch requests subagent context defaults, Agent message wakeups and fork-prefix preservation while leaving Code Mode transport and tool ordering native-owned; it omits the removed description-first option.
Current product scope includes separate Project, Agent and Work records, scoped peer Collaboration and native helper execution in the current schema and protocol 4.9.

Native per-conversation permissions and optional bounded private review observations are implemented; Guardian no longer overrides all conversations' reviewer preferences, and missing action associations stay explicit without selecting the Guardian V3 experiment.

Retained integration repairs reconcile unassigned native Project membership and retain native child-input receipts for permitted V2 nested Work attribution without changing native V2 defaults or adding another executor; native identity, membership and Decodex presentation passed separate installed qualification, while official desktop Project presentation remains unobserved.

The lifecycle follow-up repairs independent native ownership, encrypted assignment attribution and Guardian history recovery without another executor or reviewer; later installed development qualification repairs independent-Agent conversation controls and input routing and retains distinct artifact, data-preservation and test-cleanup limits.

The product exposes read-only native memory summary, exact collaboration reply and contribution history, and retained native usage in existing desktop surfaces through protocol 4.9. Native execution and explicit Work assessment retain their owners; missing and shared attribution remain explicit.

In the earlier six-item review, items 1–3 are delivered and item 4 selected persistent attached branches; item 5 waits for upstream maturity and item 6 is deferred. Attached creation sends no input, copies no Goal and adds no automatic follow-up, scheduling, result merge or deletion policy.

Persistent attached branches expose only their own turns while native inference retains the reviewed parent context and saved source turn IDs retain boundary provenance. The retained public workflow already requires paginated source history.

The later manual review approved and delivered original items 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12 and 15 as bounded desktop refinements. Original items 13 and 31 remain undecided in the board-only native messaging issue and do not change native collaboration availability.

Original item 28 selects the current native catalog default after an explicit model retirement deadline, through existing new-Agent settings and idle recovery paths. Missing entries or upgrade suggestions alone do not cause migration; desktop cycling no longer uses a fixed model or effort list.

The user excludes diagnostic-log upload for privacy. Queue-navigation keys, copy-on-select and additional semantic range-copy gestures are not selected; clipboard latency work needs a reproduced defect, and current copy behavior stays supported.
The explicit EGM Component controls invoke the original native plugin lifecycle without reopening generic plugin management through the Agent bridge.

Optional native next-message suggestions apply to eligible completed visible answers and an empty root composer. The latest eligible answer can be reconsidered after reopening or enabling suggestions. Tab accepts a current suggestion as an undoable unsent draft and preserves ordinary navigation elsewhere.
Independent account observations and reset-credit requests remain owned by the Decodex account API client; only model activation uses its optional native policy profile.

Original item 29 is selected as a native per-server catalog-readiness switch. Settings > Agents > Context defaults edits only an existing user-configured server's startup_readiness as catalog or connection; it adds no global enablement or cache implementation. The executed exact-artifact test qualifies configuration roundtrips and preserves server transport and context thresholds, without cache-performance or installed-app acceptance.

Original items 39, 42, 50, 65 and 78 select shared Decodex branding, working-text motion, the live never-dispatched reconnect slot, bounded retained-history Find and source-labelled native child model metadata. Deferred research does not authorize implementation or daily maintenance debt.

The existing Decodex warning system covers original item 36 with exact content/identity dismissal until change or recovery. Items 32, 33, 37, 40, 52, 54, 56 and 81 are excluded; standalone Codex startup diagnostics and diagnostic export/upload controls are outside product scope. Decodex integration diagnostics, normal warnings and ordinary Markdown export remain retained.

Original item35 selects exact native historical-item navigation in the main conversation, reusing loaded records or reading bounded same-turn anchor pages with a fixed return action and no per-message nearby-history buttons. Items43,67 and72 retain collapsed-output counts, registered-resource owner lookup and existing cost estimates; resource lookup adds no historical upload scan or adoption, and estimates add no account sum or local price engine.

The work browser offers Fork for locally managed conversation rows, selects the user input in the latest completed full native turn and reuses explicit AfterTurn confirmation. Navigation and cancellation preserve drafts; creation sends no input and does not adopt unmanaged inventory rows.

Original item74 uses independent saved status filters in the existing conversation browser and Project-grouped Work list. It preserves displayed status facts, Project/search predicates, exact navigation, drafts and Work detail ownership. Its retained contract records original qualification limits; it adds no model grouping, execution policy or native runtime change.

Native Guardian root handoff context and JSON transcript mode remain deferred in issues for original items 49 and 79. A deferred issue does not authorize implementation, a setting, experimental activation or daily maintenance work.

Compatibility maintenance for original items 45, 48, 55, 60, 73, 75 and 76 is limited to actual Decodex consumers. Native algorithms, enforcement and execution keep their owner; optional modes are not activated automatically, and source inspection alone does not qualify item-76 caller attribution.

Deferred mailbox research for manual item27 is tracked in issue2562 and remains last in research order. The earlier deferred Guardian V3 and custom managed configuration choices are tracked in issues2563 and2564. Conditional cross-process MCP sharing and complete critical-path research retain issues2524 and2525. These issue links preserve deferred decisions and authorize no implementation or daily maintenance obligation.

The Side chat presentation places the source and multiple open native attached forks in the conversation header. The + action prepares the selected conversation's latest completed turn and opens a Side chat without a second confirmation or a message send, preserves per-conversation drafts, and hides a closed tab without deleting its branch.

The manual Ask separately popover, toolbar and menu entries are removed. Completed-response and text-selection actions open an attached Side chat with the referenced passage in its ordinary unsent draft. The source draft stays separate and follow-up messages use the normal composer.

Native Codex retains the saved configured provider after a default-provider change. The existing user-approved explicit recovery action still requires a live native modelProviderMismatch; its source preparation and durable fork receipt preserve history and draft, and creation sends no input.

The user deferred HumanCommand mandatory one-time command approval support in issue 2585 because there is no current product need. It is not daily implementation debt, requires a new user decision, remains unadvertised, and does not waive native enforcement or runtime qualification.
Manual catch-up pauses the maintenance owner; internal-duty resumption requires explicit user authorization. The former desktop definition stays paused while Decodex owns the workload.

Next-message suggestions retain native thread/sample, which obtains one response from a temporary inherited fork without tool execution or parent input and leaves cleanup to native Codex. Persistent Side chats use thread/fork with attachToSource and normal subsequent turns.

Automatic conversation topics use isolated native structured requests and native naming, generate after the first eligible completed user exchange and review after seven more exchanges. The source tab stays Main and Side chats display topics independently of Agent identity.
Users can create persistent Agents directly, and the selected Assistant can create them under an exact delivered user delegation without a separate helper executor.

Codex upstream maintenance is declared as an independent Decodex Agent duty with a dedicated managed worktree and daily UTC cadence. It does not select personal Assistant Memory; registration and real execution require native acceptance.

The current fixed source review and exact signed-artifact qualification are separate portable evidence. Experimental shared MCP diagnostics passed one of four cases and sharing remains disabled with a pending adaptation; generic upstream CI failures are not counted as local passing proof.
